text: Git branching is a core part of version control, allowing developers to work on new ideas without disrupting the main codebase. Typically, you create a *feature branch* from the main branch to develop a specific function or fix. Once your work is complete and tested, you can merge it back into the main branch. In team workflows, this is often done through a *pull request*, where other developers review your changes before they are integrated. This process keeps the main branch stable and makes collaboration smoother. By using branches, you can experiment freely, track changes clearly, and avoid conflicts, making version control much more efficient and organized.
